registered: 2026-11-06 ~11:05 ET, before any forward data: outcomes.jsonl has only 3 closed rows with rs_* fields (CRWV 09:48, SMCI 10:21, IREN 10:22) and they are EXCLUDED from the read (they suggested the hypothesis).
operator: 2026-11-06: 'Is there any other criteria that we can identify these and distinguish them from CRMV', then 'yes' to pre-registering run efficiency as a hypothesis.
question: Do desk entries that follow a choppy, stalled run (low efficiency over the previous 15 minutes) go never-green more often than entries that follow a clean run, and does refusing them raise the mean of the kept trades?
origin_evidence: EXPLORATORY, 3 trades, 11/06: CRWV (won +57 bp) rs_er15 0.46; SMCI (-62 bp, never green) 0.28 after ~10 minutes at 28.9-29.1; IREN (-83 bp, never green) 0.20, drifting 21.3-21.7. Run SIZE (rs_rise15_bp) did not separate them (CRWV was the largest). Not evidence: n = 3 and chosen after seeing them.
measure: rs_er15 = |close[-1] - close[0]| / sum |close[i] - close[i-1]| over the last 15 closed one-minute bars (1 = straight line, 0 = pure chop), stamped at entry by ai_entry_watch._range_shape_fields from the in-memory IEX bar store. Missing = not counted (counted separately).
primary_hypothesis: FLAG = entries in the BOTTOM third of rs_er15 on the read sample (cut = the 1/3 rank value of the read sample, computed without outcomes and printed; it becomes the gate value if it passes). ONE hypothesis.
data: Desk regular-session entries from 2026-11-06 12:00 ET onward with rs_er15 present (the three suggesting trades are before the start). Never-green = peak_price < entry + 5 bp. Net = (exit - entry)/entry bp - 3 bp. Same de-duplication as the other forward readers.
read_when: Once, at the first nightly run with >= 150 such entries. Counts only before that.
multiplicity: Three 'why do these fail' hypotheses read the same forward entries: rs_pos30 >= 0.80 (z bar 1.64, registered 11/05), rs_rise15_bp top third (z bar 1.96, registered 11/06 05:45), and this one. The family is three, so this one uses one-sided z >= 2.13 (alpha 0.0167). The two earlier bars are NOT changed after the fact; the read prints all three with the family count, and a result that only clears its own bar while failing the family bar is reported as 'single-test pass, family fail'.

pass.never_green: FLAG never-green rate above the rest in BOTH halves (split by date at the median session) and pooled one-sided z >= 2.13
pass.payoff: mean net of the kept group (not FLAG) above the mean net of all entries in BOTH halves, and the day-clustered bootstrap (2,000 resamples of sessions, seed 1106) 5th percentile of (kept - all) > 0
pass.volatility_confound: FLAG's never-green rate still above the rest inside rs_rng15_bp terciles (>= 2 of 3 positive)
pass.not_just_size: reported (information, no pass): the same split inside rs_rise15_bp top third and rest, and inside dwell_sec < 60 s vs >= 60 s, so the read says whether efficiency adds anything beyond run size or time on the board

if_pass: result-skeptic review of the positive, then a default-off gate (refuse arms with rs_er15 <= the printed cut) tested through tools/sweep_replays.py screen + confirm and the ship rule; never straight to live.
if_fail: Close; no other window, cut or normalisation of the efficiency measure is tried as a primary afterwards. Record in the running list and memory.
caveats: Never-green depends on hold length; exits are unchanged during the read (any exit config change is named in the read).
IEX bars: efficiency from sparse IEX minute closes can read as chop on thin names for feed reasons alone; the rng15 terciles partly control this.
Refusing a third of entries also cuts a third of trades; the payoff test is the one that matters (operator: profit over win rate).
tool: tools/studies/run_efficiency_forward.py (nightly via scripts/nightly.sh, counts only until due)
status: READY to log; read not before 150 forward entries

amended_feed.when: 2026-11-06 ~12:40 ET, before any SIP-period entry exists and before any of these tests was read (operator 'yes' to the SIP amendment).
amended_feed.why: The logged range, efficiency, run-size and slope measures come from the in-memory 1-minute bar store: IEX bars until the SIP flip (planned for the first SIP regular session, Tuesday 2026-11-10), SIP bars after. Denser SIP bars change what 'choppy' or 'top of range' reads as, so the two periods are not comparable.
amended_feed.rule: Entries are assigned to the IEX sample (entry time before docs/studies/feed_regime.json sip_from_et, or all entries while it is null) or the SIP sample (at or after it). The two samples are NEVER pooled. The test is read ONCE, on the first sample whose entry count reaches this prereg's minimum (ordered by entry time); the other sample is information only and does not change the verdict. All other rules (hypothesis, cuts computed on the read sample, bars, family size, extension rule) apply unchanged to the read sample.
amended_feed.flip_time: sip_from_et is set in the same step that flips alpaca_bar_feed to sip (docs/SIP_DAY1_RUNBOOK.md); tools/sip_sunday_check.py refuses GO while the feed is sip and it is null. If SIP is not bought or the flip slips, every entry stays in the IEX sample and the read is on IEX as originally written.
amended_feed.tool: tools/studies/feed_regime.py (shared), counts printed per sample nightly; tests/test_feed_regime.py.
